**January 2017:**

*   27 January: A 1947 [Chance-Vought F4U-5N Corsair](http://www.warbirdalley.com/f4u.htm), VH-III (Bu.No. 124493), landed with its landing gear retracted at Maitland Aerodrome, Rutherford, NSW, Australia. Video footage shows the aircraft stopping quickly on the grass runway. The pilot was not injured, and damage to the aircraft appears to be minimal. Discussions about the cause of the incident center around a possible loss of hydraulic pressure. \[[Video of the incident>>](https://youtu.be/fXNBA4KyZfo)\]
    
*   A restored [Mitsubishi A6M Zero Model 22](http://www.warbirdalley.com/zero.htm) was flown from Kanoya Air Base in Japan, after a long restoration. The aircraft was purchased by Japanese businessman Masahiro Ishizuka, and two test flights were performed by test pilot Skip Holm. \[[News report>>](http://www.cnn.com/2016/01/28/world/restored-japanese-zero-fighter-plane-flies-over-japan/index.html)\]
    
*   29 January: A [UTVA 66](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utva_66), YU-DLL (c/n51102), made a forced landing in a field near Eschbronn-Mariazell, Germany after apparently running out of fuel, and was substantially damaged in the hard landing. The pilot suffered head and neck injuries. \[[News report>>](http://www.schwarzwaelder-bote.de/inhalt.eschbronn-pilot-bei-notlandung-schwer-verletzt.d5d095c5-8d0c-4283-bc5b-1df8d0e2bb3b.html)\]
    

**February 2017:**

*   4 February: A 1942 [deHavilland DH.82A Tiger Moth](http://www.warbirdalley.com/tiger.htm), G-ANSM (c/n 82909) made a forced landing in a field near Peterborough, Cambridgeshire, UK. Damage to the airplane appears to be minor. There is conflicting information about injuries to the pilot.
    
*   6 February: A modified [North American T-6 Texan called a "Super-6,"](http://www.warbirdalley.com/t6.htm) N426KS, crashed near Morganton, North Carolina, USA, after suffering engine problems. The owner/pilot was allegedly rescued from the fiery crash by two local residents. \[[Local news report>>](http://www.wsoctv.com/news/local/small-plane-crash-reported-in-burke-county/491580885)\]
    
*   11 February: A [Beechcraft T-34B Mentor](http://www.warbirdalley.com/t34.htm), N18PS, left the paved surface of the runway while landing in St. Petersburg, Florida, USA. Neither the pilot nor passenger were injured, but the aircraft appears to have sustained damage to at least its landing gear, propeller, and engine. \[[Local report>>](http://wfla.com/2017/02/11/small-plane-crash-reported-at-st-pete-airport/)\]
    
*   14 February: A [Yakovlev Yak-52](http://www.warbirdalley.com/yak52.htm), G-CBSS, made an emergency landing near Couvin, Belgium after an engine problem. The pilot suffered a broken leg, and the airplane was damaged beyond repair.
    
*   16 February: A 1957 [Beechcraft T-34A Mentor](http://www.warbirdalley.com/t34.htm), N3434G, clipped trees and crashed at a private airfield near Vada, Georgia, USA. The owner/pilot was killed and the aircraft was substantially damaged. \[[Local news report>>](http://www.wctv.tv/content/news/Decatur-County-plane-crash-414022343.html)\]
    
*   18 February: The Dixie Wing of the Commemorative Air Force is pleased to announce the first flight of their [Bell P-63A Kingcobra](http://www.warbirdalley.com/p63.htm) in over 40 years, including 16 years of restoration. The aircraft, N191H (s/n 42-68941) was retired as a test aircraft and sold off the military roster in 1946, and is one of only four flyable P-63s in the world. \[[Dixie Wing P-63 article and photos>>](http://dixiewing.org/2017/02/20/p-63a-flies/)\]
    
*   23 February: A 1976 [Aero Vodochody L-39 Albatros](http://www.warbirdalley.com/l39.htm), VH-KVZ, came to rest in the grass next to the runway with its nose gear and left main landing gear retracted at Bankstown Airport near Sydney, Australia. Reports differ on whether the aircraft was taking off or landing at the time. Neither the pilot nor passenger were injured. The aircraft appears to be mostly undamaged, but fire crews appeared to be cleaning up some spilled fuel from the incident. \[[Local news report>>](https://au.news.yahoo.com/a/34490775/mig-fighter-aircraft-crashes-in-sydneys-south-west/)\]
    

**March 2017:**

*   1 March: A [deHavilland DH-82A Tiger Moth](http://www.warbirdalley.com/tiger.htm), ZK-BRM, struck an obstruction on takeoff near Blenheim, New Zealand, which apparently detached one of the main landing gear wheels. The aircraft then returned for a landing, which resulted in the aircraft coming to rest on its belly in a dry riverbed. Neither the pilot nor the passenger were injured \[[News report>>](http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/89952508/plane-crash-lands-at-omaka)\]
    
*   14 March: Noted warbird collector/pilot and businessman Thomas Friedkin passed away at age 81. Mr. Friedkin appeared in several movies as both a helicopter pilot and fixed-wing pilot. *   27 March: An [Aero Vodochody L-29 Delfin](http://www.warbirdalley.com/l29.htm), OM-JLP, landed with its landing gear retracted at Silač, Slovakia. Neither the pilot nor the passenger were injured, and the aircraft appeared to suffer only minor damage. \[[News report>>](http://www.vydavatelstvo-mps.sk/letectvi-kosmonautika/480-nudzove-pristatie-civilneho-l-29-na-sliaci.html)\]

*   1 April: A 1944 [North American SNJ-5 Texan](http://www.warbirdalley.com/t6.htm), N29965 (c/n 90634), made a forced landing in a field near Punta Gorda, Florida, USA after an engine malfunction. The pilot was not injured, and the passenger suffered only a minor scratch on his arm. Damage to the aircraft is unknown. \[[Local news report>>](http://www.winknews.com/2017/04/01/plane-crash-lands-near-punta-gorda-airport/)\]
    
*   8 April: A 1949 [North American T-6G Texan](http://www.warbirdalley.com/t6.htm), N3167G (s/n 49-3272), ended up on its back after landing in Culpeper, Virginia, USA. Law enforcement officials said the aircraft ran off the side of the runway and overturned. Both the pilot and passenger were taken to local hospitals with undetermined injuries. The aircraft was substantially damaged. \[[News report>>](http://www.fauquier.com/news/pilot-passenger-injured-in-culpeper-plane-crash/article_32f8681a-1c98-11e7-80e6-23e00dae5078.html)\]

*   19 April: A [North American SNJ-5 Texan](http://www.warbirdalley.com/t6.htm), N7969C (s/n 42-84535), suffered a loss of directional control on landing in Van Nuys, California, USA. *   29 April: A 1983 [Yakovlev Yak-52](http://www.warbirdalley.com/yak52.htm), N132MD (c/n 833802), made a forced landing in a vineyard near Porterville, California, USA, after losing engine power. The pilot and passenger were killed, and the aircraft was destroyed. \[[News link>>](http://www.kmbc.com/article/two-killed-in-plane-crash-in-atchison-kan/10313990)\]  \[_Editor's note:_ It's tough to report on accidents, but it's especially hard when the pilot is a close friend and mentor. **January 2018:**

*   17 January: A [Bell UH-1H "Huey"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bell_UH-1_Iroquois) helicopter, N658H (s/n 67-17658), crashed near Raton, New Mexico, USA, killing five of the six people on board. \[[News link>>](https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/news/uk/steam-car-record-holder-among-five-killed-in-helicopter-crash-36506428.html)\]
    
*   31 January: The 1944 [Douglas C-47 Skytrain](http://www.warbirdalley.com/c47.htm), N88874 (s/n #42-92847) that led the Normandy, France invasion on June 6, 1944 has flown once again, after a long restoration. The aircraft, named _"That's All, Brother,"_ made its post-restoration flight from Oshkosh, Wisconsin, USA, where it was stored in a field ten years ago. It will be operated by the Central Texas Wing of the Commemorative Air Force. It is slated to appear in many stateside events before marking the 75th Anniversary of D-Day by flying across the Atlantic to the UK and Normandy. \[[CAF news brief>>](https://commemorativeairforce.org/rss/694-wwii-aircraft-that-led-the-d-day-invasion-flies-again)\]

*   3 November: A [Siai-Marchetti SF260D](http://www.warbirdalley.com/sf260.htm), I-ISAE, crashed in a field near Caorle, Italy. Both occupants were killed, although the aircraft remained largely intact and there was no fire. \[[Local news>>](https://www.rainews.it/tgr/fvg/video/2018/11/fvg-aereo-caduto-caorle-incidente-morto-professore-units-universita-trieste-8a4023fc-86d8-468d-ae31-34ca6430d9da.html)\]
    
*   17 November: A [North American P-51D Mustang](http://www.warbirdalley.com/p51.htm), N4132A (s/n 44-74445)(_"Pecos Bill"_), crashed in a parking lot next to an apartment complex near Fredericksburg, Texas, USA, after an apparent engine failure. Owner/pilot Cowden Ward and his WWII-veteran passenger and former B-17 bombardier, Vince Losada, were killed. The aircraft had participated in a flyover as part of a history program for a nearby museum, and the owner was known to give rides to WWII veterans. \[[Local news report>>](https://www.kxan.com/news/texas/pilot-who-honored-veterans-id-d-in-deadly-fredericksburg-plane-crash/1603904380)\]
    
*   22 November: A long-lost [Supermarine Spitfire](http://www.warbirdalley.com/spit.htm) reconnaissance plane was discovered in good condition in a mountain bog in Norway by a UK-based researcher. Its pilot, Alastair Gunn, was on a long-range photo mission from Scotland when he was shot down in 1942. Later, he was a part of the famous "Great Escape" from the _Stalag Luft 3_ prison camp, but was executed by his captors in April 1944. In his memory, Spitfire AA810 will be restored to flying condition, and a television documentary of the aircraft's recovery and restoration is being produced. \[[More information>>](https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/spitfire-norway-mountain-great-escape-pilot-found-second-world-war-nazi-raf-espionage-alastair-gunn-a8646841.html)\]
    
*   30 November: A [Scottish Aviation Bulldog](http://www.warbirdalley.com/bulldog.htm), HA-TVD, struck powerlines and crashed near Rábapaty, Hungary. The pilot was killed and the aircraft was destroyed. \[[Local news>>](https://airportal.hu/lezuhant-egy-kisrepulogep-sarvar-kozeleben/)\]
    

**December 2018:**

*   8 December: One [DeHavilland DH-100 Vampire](http://www.warbirdalley.com/vampire.htm) was destroyed and another one severely damaged in a hangar fire at the Paris-Villaroche Airport, France. \[[News link>>](http://www.leparisien.fr/seine-et-marne-77/seine-et-marne-deux-avions-de-collection-en-feu-a-melun-villaroche-08-12-2018-7963572.php)\]
    
*   12 December: The pilot of a 1958 [Hawker Hunter Mk.58](http://www.warbirdalley.com/hunter.htm), N323AX, operated by a defense contractor, ejected from the aircraft after takeoff from Honolulu, Hawaii, USA. The pilot sustained back injuries and was rescued by the Coast Guard and local boaters. The aircraft was destroyed. \[[Local news, including videos>>](https://www.hawaiinewsnow.com/2018/12/13/rescuers-responding-reports-military-aircraft-crash-off-honolulu/)\]
    
*   31 December: A [North American XP-82 Twin Mustang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_American_F-82_Twin_Mustang) N887XP (s/n 44-83887), the only one currently airworthy, made its first post-restoration flight in Douglas, Georgia, USA. Restorer Tom Reilly and his team acquired parts of the aircraft from a private collection in 2008, as well as from numerous and diverse other sources. Today's 5-minute flight was actually an accidental flight, intended to be only a high-speed taxi and a brief liftoff. \[[More information>>](http://www.xp-82twinmustangproject.com/)\]

**January 2019:**

ZK-BCV (PZ474), owned by collector Rod Lewis, made its first post-restoration flight in Auckland, New Zealand. There are now four airworthy examples of the type. Congratulations to Avspecs, Ltd on their accomplishment! \[[More information>>](http://www.warbirdrestoration.co.nz/)\]
    
*   21 January: A 1942 AMI DC-3-65TP (formerly [Douglas C-47A Dakota](http://www.warbirdalley.com/c47.htm)) N467KS (s/n 43-15709) struck powerlines and trees, and crashed shortly after takeoff in Apple Creek, Ohio, USA. Both pilots were killed, and the aircraft was substantially destroyed. The aircraft was a turbine conversion of a vintage DC-3. Initial reports suggest the aircraft may have had engine troubles before the crash. _\[Editor's Note: We are sad to report that one of the pilots was Brian Stoltzfus, owner of Preferred Airparts, a noted supplier of parts in the warbird industry, as well as a well-known restoration and maintenance shop. The two occupants of the floatplane received minor injuries, and the aircraft was substantially damaged. \[[News link>>](https://www.record-bee.com/2019/09/10/seaplane-crashes-into-lake-at-splash-in/)\]
    
*   14 September: The crew of a [Douglas C-47 Dakota III](http://www.warbirdalley.com/c47.htm), XA947, operated by the RAF's Battle of Britain Memorial Flight, performed a successful emergency landing in Manchester, UK, after experiencing engine problems with their left engine. The aircraft was undamaged. \[[News link>>](https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/live-manchester-airport-emergency-landing-16919754)\]
    
*   19 September: A 1949 [North American T-6G Texan](http://www.warbirdalley.com/t6.htm), N799MU (s/n 49-3368), made a belly landing in a farm field near Blountstown, Florida, USA after an engine failure. The aircraft was damaged, but the two occupants were not injured. \[[Local news>>](https://www.wjhg.com/content/news/Plane-crash-lands-in-Calhoun-County-both-people-inside-safe-560810061.html)\]
    
*   21 September: A [Cessna L-19 Bird Dog](http://www.warbirdalley.com/l19.htm), D-ECII, was substantially damaged during an apparent landing at a model airfield in the Czech Republic. The status of the pilot is unknown.
    
*   21 September: A [Supermarine Spitfire Mk VIII](http://www.warbirdalley.com/spit.htm), D-FEUR (c/n 6S-583793) suffered a propeller strike on takeoff from Duxford, Cambridgeshire, UK. The aircraft was substantially damaged.
    

**October 2019:**

*   2 October: A 1944 [Boeing B-17G Flying Fortress](http://www.warbirdalley.com/b17.htm), N93012 (_"Nine O Nine"_), operated by the Collings Foundation, was destroyed during an emergency landing at Bradley, Connecticut, USA, with the loss of seven of the thirteen people on board. The crew of the aircraft was giving rides as part of the foundation's "Wings of Freedom" tour, when they reported engine problems shortly after takeoff, and began making their way back to the airport. The aircraft crashed short of the runway and came to rest against some buildings holding the airport's de-icing fluid farm. The Pilot in Command of the aircraft was believed to be the highest-time B-17 pilot in the country. \[_Editor's note:_ The implications of this tragedy are not yet known, but within two days of the incident, politicians began calling for more scrutiny and tighter regulations on warbird operations in the USA. Pease stay involved to keep warbirds in the air, where they belong. And please support the Collings Foundation in their difficult time. Our condolences to the families and friends of those lost. \[[News link>>](https://www.courant.com/breaking-news/hc-br-windsor-locks-bradley-international-airport-plane-crash-20191002-jfkph65krrfhxlrlb3eehksdiu-story.html)\]
    
*   4 October: Dr. Tony Buechler, a noted P-51 Mustang owner (_"Petie 2nd"_) and philanthropist, passed away at the age of 67. \[[EAA News>>](https://www.eaa.org/eaa/news-and-publications/eaa-news-and-aviation-news/news/10-10-2019-Gone-West-Tony-Buechler)\]
    
*   5 October: A [Yakovlev Yak-52](http://www.warbirdalley.com/yak52.htm), LY-WAA, was involved in an accident at Banesti Airfield, Prahova County, Romania. No injuries were reported.
    
*   16 October: A Yakovlev Yak-18T, F-HYAC, crashed near Draguignan, France after a serious mechanical issue. Neither occupant was injured. \[[News link>>](https://www.varmatin.com/faits-divers/video-un-avion-atterrit-durgence-a-draguignan-apres-un-probleme-mecanique-a-plus-de-1000m-daltitude-422914)\]
    
*   18 October: A 1945 [Douglas DC-3](http://www.warbirdalley.com/c47.htm), N437GB, operated by a cargo airline, crashed into the water during an approach to an airport near Nassau, Bahamas. The two crewmembers survived and were rescued by the Bahamian military. \[[News link>>](https://wsvn.com/news/us-world/uscg-2-people-ok-after-cargo-plane-crashes-north-of-nassau/)\]
    
*   21 October: A 1959 [Hawker Hunter MK.58](http://www.warbirdalley.com/hunter.htm), N344AX, operated by a US defense contractor, suffered a runway incursion at Newport News, Virginia, USA, after an apparent mechanical issue. The pilot was not injured. \[[Local news>>](https://www.13newsnow.com/article/news/local/mycity/newport-news/military-plane-crashed-at-newport-newswilliamsburg-airport-after-landing-gear-issue/291-4239dffc-f5ef-4d6b-9d9b-699fc6ef762b)\]
    
*   22 October: A 1987 [Antonov/PZL AN-2](http://www.warbirdalley.com/an2.htm), N87AN, sustained minor damage after performing a forced landing on a road near Bishop, California, USA. Neither of the occupants was injured.
    

**November 2019:**

*   1 November: A [Grumman OV-1 Mohawk](http://www.warbirdalley.com/ov1.htm), N10VD, crashed during an airshow in Stuart, Florida. USA. The pilot was killed, and the aircraft was destroyed. \[[News link>>](https://www.wptv.com/news/region-martin-county/stuart/plane-crash-at-stuart-air-show)\]
    
*   14 November: a 1958 [North American Rockwell FJ-4B Fury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_American_FJ-4_Fury), N4--FS (BuNo 143575) ended up on its belly after landing in Richfield, Utah, USA. *   1 March: In the wake of the worldwide Covid-19 outbreak, numerous airshows and public aviation events have been cancelled or postponed. In additional, most museums and collections are closed. For an updated list of cancellations and postponements, visit the AirshowStuff website [here](https://airshowstuff.com/v4/2020/numerous-airshows-cancel-in-the-face-of-coronavirus-pandemic-here-is-a-full-list/).
    
*   25 March: The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has ruled that the Collings Foundation, whose B-17 bomber crashed last fall, can no longer carry passengers due to the FAA's concerns about safety. \[[More information>>](https://www.courant.com/news/connecticut/hc-news-faa-says-collings-foundation-cannot-carry-passengers-20200325-twq2alj7i5gztllf6h4p22mjyi-story.html)\]
    

**April 2020:**

*   1 April: Legendary warbird pilot and safety advocate Randy Sohn passed away at the age of 86. Randy was an early member of the Commemorative Air Force (CAF), and was one of the people responsible of the rescue of the CAF's B-29 "Fifi." He held a rare "Unlimited" piston rating from the US Federal Aviation Administration, meaning he was qualified to fly _any_ high-performance piston-powered aircraft. He authored numerous advice articles for warbird pilots that were eventually assembled into collections variously called _[Randy Sohn's Round Engine Notes](https://captainbillywalker.com/aviation-history-people/randy-sohns-round-engine-notes-2011/)_ and/or _[Warbird Notes](http://www.douglasdc3.com/sohn/warbird.htm)._ These articles helped countless pilots learn the unique characteristics of vintage airplanes. \[[Randy's full obituary>>](https://www.startribune.com/obituaries/detail/0000352199/?fullname=randall-lee-sohn)\]
    
*   11 April: An unknown vandal damaged two [Douglas DC-3](http://www.warbirdalley.com/c47.htm)s on Cape Cod, Massachusetts, USA. The owner reported the elevator of one airplane, and the trim tab of the other, suffered upwards of $15,000 in damage. \[[Local news>>](https://www.capecod.com/cape-wide-news/cape-cod-airfield-offers-reward-after-vintage-dc-3s-found-vandalized/)\]
    
*   13 April: An early-morning tornado severely damaged a [Douglas C-54E/R-5D Skymaster](http://www.warbirdalley.com/c54.htm) N500EJ (c/n 27370, s/n 44-9144) (_"The Sprit of Freedom"_) parked in Walterboro, South Carolina, USA. The aircraft, operated by the Berlin Airlift Historical Foundation, was moved over 100 yards and slammed into a hangar by the storm. \[[Local news>>](https://www.live5news.com/2020/04/13/storms-damage-least-planes-walterboro-airport/)\]
    
*   26 April: A 1935 [Focke-Wulf FW 44J _"Stieglitz,"_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Focke-Wulf_Fw_44) D-ETUF, crashed near Siegen, Germany, injuring the passenger. The pilot attempted to return to the airport due to mechanical problems, but had to perform an emergency landing a few hundred meters short, whereupon the airplane hit some construction equipment. The aircraft sustained substantial damage. \[[Local news>>](https://www.ww-kurier.de/artikel/89877-alter-doppeldecker-am-siegerland-flughafen-abgestuerzt)\]
    
*   28 April: A [Hunting Jet Provost T3A](http://www.warbirdalley.com/jp.htm), N4427Q (ex-XM371), suffered an engine failure and the pilot made a forced landing near Center, Colorado, USA. The pilot was not injured, and the aircraft was reported to be undamaged.

*   2 May: A 1996 [Yakovlev Yak-52](http://www.warbirdalley.com/yak52.htm), N27YK (s/n 9611905), crashed in Palmyra, Illinois, USA under unknown circumstances. *   2 May: The pilot of a [deHavilland/Airco DH-4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airco_DH.4), N32517, walked away with no injuries after crashing the plane during a test flight in Bowling Green, Kentucky, USA. *   28 May: The late Paul Allen's magnificent collection of aircraft and vehicles, the [Flying Heritage and Combat Armor Museum](https://flyingheritage.org/) in Everett, Washington, USA, has announced that it will be closing for an indefinite period of time, due to the "devastating effect" of the COVID-19 crisis. *   28 May: A [Messerschmitt Bf 108D Taifun](http://www.warbirdalley.com/bf108.htm), D-EHAF (c/n 5253), made a belly landing after a landing gear malfunction. Neither occupant was injured. *   21 September: A 1943 [Boeing E75 Stearman](http://www.warbirdalley.com/pt17.htm), N1524M (s/n 75-8060), made a forced landing into wooded terrain near Honea Path, South Carolina, USA, following a loss of engine power. **October 2020:**

*   10 October: A [Nanchang CJ-6](http://www.warbirdalley.com/cj6.htm), C-FTCJ, made an intentional gear-up landing at Victoria BC, Canada, after the pilot reported the landing gear would not come down. The aircraft sustained relatively minor damage, and the pilot was not injured. \[[News link>>](https://vancouverisland.ctvnews.ca/small-plane-makes-emergency-landing-on-grass-at-victoria-airport-1.5141655)\]
    
*   11 October: A 1949 [North American T-6G Texan](http://www.warbirdalley.com/t6.htm), N821DS, made a belly landing in Mesa, Arizona, USA, after the pilot reported a hydraulic problem. The aircraft suffered some minor damage, but the two pilots on board were not injured. \[[News link, with video of the incident>>](https://www.azfamily.com/news/aircraft-makes-belly-landing-at-falcon-field-in-mesa/article_aeed7210-0c10-11eb-aeff-d711fca010c1.html)\]
    
*   13 October: A [deHavilland DH.82 Tiger Moth](http://www.warbirdalley.com/tiger.htm), OH-XLA (c/n 85167), ended up on its back after a landing accident in Nurmijärvi, Finland. The aircraft was substantially damaged, but the two occupants were not seriously injured. \[[Local news>>](https://yle.fi/uutiset/3-11427112)\]
    
*   18 October: A 1982 [Aero Vodochody L-39C Albatros](http://www.warbirdalley.com/l39.htm), N699BA, made a gear-up landing in Montgomery, New York, USA. The aircraft sustained moderate damage, but neither occupant was injured.
    

**November 2020:**

*   8 November: Prominent warbird pilot, restorer and owner of [Ezell Aviation](http://www.ezellaviation.com/) Nelson Ezell passed away. In the business since 1986, Nelson and his talented company were responsible for many exemplary aircraft restorations over the years, including Corsairs, Sea Furies, Mustangs, Bearcats, Lightnings, and more. In 2015, he was inducted into the EAA Warbirds of America Hall of Fame. In 2017, he was seriously injured in the crash of a Sea Fury.
    
*   28 November: A 1936 [Ryan PT-20 (ST-A)](http://www.warbirdalley.com/pt22.htm), N14984, suffered a propeller-strike during a landing in Modesto, California, USA. Damage to the aircraft appeared to be minimal.
    

**December 2020:**

*   After nearly 40 years of service with the Boeing corporation, the company's two [Lockheed T-33](http://www.warbirdalley.com/tbird.htm) chase planes are being retired. The company announced the 66-year old jets would be replaced with something else due to maintenance supply-chain problems.
    

**February 2021:**

*   2 February: An [Aeronca 65-TC Defender](http://www.warbirdalley.com/l3.htm), N27336, made a runways excursion after landing in Barstow, Oklahoma, USA. The aircraft was not damaged and the pilot was not injured.
    
*   12 February: A [Boeing B75 Stearman](http://www.warbirdalley.com/pt17.htm), N1450HP, suffered an engine failure while performing aerobatics, and the pilot performed an emergency landing in the desert near Gold Canyon, Arizona, USA. The pilot was not injured, and the aircraft was not damaged.
    
*   15 February: A [North American SNJ-6 Texan](http://www.warbirdalley.com/t6.htm), N452WQ, experienced a ground loop and runway excursion after landing in Kissimmee, Florida, USA. The aircraft suffered minor damage, but neither of the pilots was injured.
    
*   22 February: A 1942 [North American AT-6C Texan](http://www.warbirdalley.com/t6.htm), N42GK, suffered the collapse of its landing gear while taxiing at Pompano Beach, Florida, USA. Neither the pilot nor the passenger were injured. \[[Local news link, with several errors>>](https://wsvn.com/news/local/broward/wwii-fighter-plane-replica-damaged-after-landing-gear-fails-at-pompano-beach-airpark/)\]
    
*   23 February: The Flying Leatherneck Museum, a collection of military aircraft located at MCAS Miramar in California, has announced that it is closing soon. The museum director gave "finances" as the reason for the closure. It is not known what will happen to the collection. \[[News link >>](https://www.10news.com/news/local-news/san-diego-news/mcas-miramar-flying-leatherneck-museum-to-close-permanently)\]
    
*   25 February: A [Dassault Mirage F1B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dassault_Mirage_F1), N601AX, operated by defense contractor Airborne Tactical Advantage Company (ATAC), was reported to have had a landing gear issue that resulted in a belly landing at Tyndall AFB, Florida, USA. During the incident, one pilot ejected and the other remained with the airplane -- both survived, but are reported to have been injured. The aircraft was seen on a tracking website to have taken off, then spent some time circling over the Gulf of Mexico before returning to base, implying a possible landing gear anomaly. \[[Article at "The Drive" site >>](https://www.thedrive.com/the-war-zone/39472/contractor-flown-mirage-f1-aggressor-crash-lands-at-tyndall-air-force-base-reports)\]
    
*   28 February: An Aero Vodochody L-39C Albatros, N43722, made a gear-up landing at St. Petersburg, Florida, USA. Neither occupant of the airplane were injured. The aircraft sustained moderate damage.
    

**March 2021:**

*   5 March: An [Aermacchi MB-326M (Atlas Impala Mk II)](http://www.warbirdalley.com/mb326.htm), N155TP, operated by the National Test Pilot School, crashed into open desert near Edwards AFB, California. The two pilots successfully ejected.
    
*   17 March: General Des Barker, a test pilot, prolific safety advisor, and author of two influential books about airshow/display flying safety, died along with another pilot in the crash of a rare [Patchen Explorer](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Patchen_TSC-2_Explorer_%E2%80%982000%E2%80%99_/(ZU-UGF/)_/(16670648338/).jpg) near Swartkop Air Force Base, South Africa. The aircraft was operated by the South African Air Force Museum. Both pilots were highly experienced. Among other works, Barker wrote _"Zero Error Margin"_ in 2003, by far the most comprehensive written examination of high-performance display flying in existence. His newest book was _"Anatomy of Airshow Accidents."_  \[[News link>>](https://www.defenceweb.co.za/aerospace/aerospace-aerospace/saaf-museum-patchen-explorer-in-fatal-crash/)\]  _\[Ed. Note: General Barker's influence in the airshow community was huge, and he will be missed. Our condolences to his family, friends and associates.\]_

A RETIRED senior RAF pilot from Warwickshire was one of three people killed in two plane crashes within 24 hours at the same air show....
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

![Image 1](https://i2-prod.coventrytelegraph.net/article2987665.ece/ALTERNATES/s1200e/000D92D6-4C58-1B1B-BCDE80C328EC05F2.jpg)

A RETIRED senior RAF pilot from Warwickshire was one of three people killed in two plane crashes within 24 hours at the same air show.

The tragedies happened at Biggin Hill airfield in Kent over the weekend.

Sir Kenneth Hayr, aged 66, from Southam, died alongside electronics engineer Jonathon Kerr on Saturday when their vintage plane spiralled out of control and hit the ground, bursting into a fireball.

A crowd of 35,000 people stood in silence as both occupants of the De Havilland Vampire were killed instantly.

The show was called off after a second horrific accident yesterday, when a 60-year-old American King Cobra went out of control and exploded into trees, killing pilot Guy Bancroft-Wilson, aged 43, a British Airways captain based at Gatwick.

Sir Kenneth was a former Air Marshall and Deputy Chief of Defence Staff, who retired in 1992. He was considered one of the best

He held senior positions in the RAF throughout the Falklands and Gulf wars, planning the RAF?s role in the Desert Storm operation, for which he received the Kuwait Liberation order (first grade) for his service in 1991 as well as the KBE.

He had a passion for flying fighter aircraft, and his hobbies were display aerobatics, paragliding pilots in the RAF.

Saturday's crash happened when the Vampire was halfway through the final display with a Vixen plane.

The 1950s former Swiss air force trainer jet had flown over the crowd four times before it corkscrewed and plummeted into a ridge.

The plane narrowly missed a row of terraced houses just 100 yards away and showered and parachuting. gardens with debris.

Sir Kenneth, who moved to the Midlands from his native New Zealand, lost his wife Joyce in 1987. They had three sons.

Biggin Hill spokesman Nick Smith said there was a feeling of shock at the show following the crashes. He said: "I have been here since 1978 working on the show and only in 1980 were there any fatalities.

"Now in two days we have lost two aircraft and we have got two lots of fatalities."

Today the Air Accidents Investigation Branch was due to start its investigation into the crashes.

Last night the family of Jonathon Kerr paid tribute to the dead men, saying: "When we as a family visited the crash site we thought it very apt as a Spitfire, Hurricane and a Lancaster flew overhead.

"I am sure that it was the most fitting tribute to both Jonathon and Sir Kenneth."

A spokeswoman for the Ministry of Defence said: "Both the MoD and the RAF are very sad to hear of Sir Kenneth's death in this tragic accident.

"Our condolences go to his family."
